title: Hopper FP8 autoswitching heuristics, validation, and temporary kernel fallback plan
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Ship a conservative, well-tested path for enabling FP8 profiles (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper-class GPUs. This ticket covers three linked efforts: (1) a diagnostic + autoswitching heuristic that chooses between E4M3 and E5M2 per-request or per-model basis using activation statistics gathered at calibration time; (2) a set of stability hardening patches and a short-term kernel fallback that disables the new FP8 kernel when a memory/overflow pattern is detected; (3) an accuracy validation campaign and rollout plan for canary customers. This work is intended to reduce rollout risk while preserving the cost/latency benefits of FP8 for compatible models.
acceptance_criteria: Autoswitching mechanism picks E4M3 or E5M2 with documented rule set and unit tests
End-to-end accuracy regression <= 1.0% relative to FP16 baseline on benchmark suite (LLM-eval-std) for enabled models
Kernel fallback triggers within 50ms for detected instability and falls back to safe variant (FP16/INT8) without losing in-flight request correctness
Calibration job produces per-model activation histograms and a confidence score used by selector
CI covers representative model families and runs on an emulated Hopper node
Canary rollout plan with automated metrics and rollback thresholds documented in the ticket
tasks: Add diagnostics mode to calibration pipeline: sample activation percentiles and peak rate
Design and implement selector heuristics (percentile thresholds + activation skew detection)
Implement light-weight runtime autoswitch that consults selector metadata at model load-time and per-request override
Create kernel fallback trigger (watcher) that detects overflow/NaN spikes and switches to safe path
Author CI integration tests with small LLMs (125M, 1.3B) to simulate activation distributions
Run accuracy validation on LLaMA2-13B, Llama-2-chat 13B, and MPT-7B across typical prompt set
Create a canary configuration in Dedicated and Hosted for 2 customers/internal teams
Write docs: console flags, rollout runbook, calibration artifacts location
Open GitHub PRs and coordinate runtime release (runtime-1.22)
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created after spike; initial design reviewed with Applied ML and Runtime teams
2025-02-11: Diagnostic schema defined (activation percentiles: 50/75/90/99, peak-rate, mean-abs);
2025-02-12: Prototype selector heuristics implemented in calibration service (branch: feat/calib-selector). Collected baseline stats on 10 models.

2025-02-14: Discovered a kernel edge-case causing NaN spikes when activation kurtosis > 12. Temporary mitigation: introduce mem-bound scaling in kernel that reduces dynamic range until further tuning.
2025-02-15: Integration test run: LLaMA2-13B perplexity delta vs FP16 = 0.6% at 512 tokens (passes threshold). Observed throughput drop ~6% when fallback engaged.
2025-02-16: Opened PRs for selector and fallback watcher; requesting runtime eng review (PRs linked below). Preparing canary rollout doc.
test_results: LLaMA2-13B: perplexity delta vs FP16 = +0.6% (512 tokens, mix of open prompts)
MPT-7B: generation BLEU-style metric drift = +0.9% (passes acceptance)
Small models (125M): selector correctly picks E4M3 for 84% of samples, E5M2 for 16%
Observed NaN spike pattern reproduced in synthetic stress test with activation kurtosis > 12 (investigation ticket created)
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary on staging for 48h with simulated traffic and metric guardrails. Stage 2: two customer canaries (low-risk) for 7 days. Metrics: request success rate, 95th latency, perplexity delta on eval-set, kernel-trigger count. Auto-rollback if success_rate drop >2% or perplexity delta >1.5% for 1h window. Stage 3: gradual 10% increments across Dedicated pools with monitoring dashboard. Full release coordinated with runtime-1.22.
risks: Undetected model families with extreme activation distributions causing silent quality regressions
Kernel fallback increases latency/CPU pressure on fallback path leading to SLO breaches
Calibration overhead for large fleets could add measurable job time and cost
Selector false negatives/positives requiring conservative thresholds that reduce FP8 utilization
dependencies: ENG-40195 (runtime kernel perf improvements - required for safe fallback)
SEC-29 (KMS key propagation for canary telemetry)
